entities.summary:
Quintus Appuleius Pansa (b. 400 BCE, Rome) was a public servant or civil administrator of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Rome. He is best known for his military leadership and service under the Roman Republic, particularly during the Cimbric War. Pansa played a significant role in the governance of the Roman province of Gaul, where he oversaw the construction of infrastructure and implemented policies aimed at maintaining Roman control.

As a prominent figure in the Roman Republic, Pansa was instrumental in shaping the military strategy and tactics employed by the Roman legions. His expertise in military leadership and administration earned him recognition among his peers and superiors, who valued his counsel and sought his advice on matters of war and state.

 Despite his significance in Roman history, Pansa's legacy has been somewhat overshadowed by that of his contemporaries. Nevertheless, his contributions to the Roman Republic's military and administrative structures remain an important part of the era's narrative.

 The inscription on the Temple of Juno on the Aventine Hill, Rome, bears an epitaph to Pansa, testifying to his enduring presence in Roman memory.
